newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc eyes correction, copper consolidating.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc eyes correction, copper consolidating.

text.p: Rallying zinc prices may correct short-term to test support between US$1,375 to $1,400 before the rally resumes and tries overhead resistance at $1,450 in the next few months, dealers said on Tuesday.
"The zinc price will test the $1,450 resistance in three months, but it may first pull back to seek support at US$1,400," one trader at a major Japanese trade house said.
Three-month zinc notched up a fresh 6-3/4-year high of $1,415 on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday, before losing ground to finish $9.50 stronger at $1,408.50.
A Singapore trader said the zinc correction could test support at US$1,375.
The Japanese trader said increased demand from the galvanised steel and car industries could push zinc to above $1,500 by year-end.
"I think zinc will reach the $1,500 level this year."

Chinese traders have reportedly shipped 5,000 tonnes of zinc to the LME's Singapore warehouse which is due to arrive soon, but most dealers shrugged off the news and said the Chinese were seeking profits between the $1,400 and $1,450 levels.
"Chinese traders are selling now, but they will start buying if zinc prices fall near or below $1,400," he said.
Trade sources said the Japanese industry was the most likely purchaser of Chinese zinc as the Japanese have taken "long bull" positions in the metal.
Traders estimated about 10,000 tonnes of zinc remains off LME warrant in Singapore.
The volume of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 28,275 tonnes on Monday, up from 25,025 tonnes a week ago and sharply up from 11,250 tonnes a month ago.

They said the shipment problems created for Chile's mining industry by severe winter blizzards and flooding was providing short-term support for three-month LME copper and the metal could test $2,550 a tonne resistance soon.
"I think the problems in Chile will give copper some support today," a Singapore trader said. "But will have only a short-term impact on the market."
He said three-month copper is likely to consolidate in a range between $2,480 to $2,550 on the LME later on Tuesday.
Aluminium traded quietly in Singapore on Tuesday and premiums for Western 20-25 kg aluminium ingots remain unchanged at US$90 a tonne.
"Aluminium is very quiet, so not much changes there," one trader said.
